safety_lead_time.comparison_action: decrease by 1.8 days vs SAP value of 3.5

narrative: Material PL2__M9CF40FE exhibits variable demand (CV=0.43) with a flat trend across 141 working days and an annual volume of ~1M units. Lead times are highly volatile (CV=0.87, range 0.03–2.95 days), making safety stock the dominant buffer component. A continuous-review (r,Q) policy was selected: the EOQ of 54,484 units is capacity-capped to 35,789, and a safety stock of 7,492 units is required to achieve the 95% service level. This policy reduces total annual inventory cost by 83% versus the current SAP MOQ-only baseline.
warnings: Volatile lead time (CV=0.87) — supplier delivery consistency requires active monitoring

Storage capacity constraint is active — EOQ capped from 54,484 to 35,789 units

research_insights.selection_rationale: Variable but non-intermittent demand (CV=0.43, 96.5% non-zero days) with known unit cost and holding rate makes EOQ-based (r,Q) the canonical choice. Continuous review is appropriate given the high lead time volatility requiring prompt reorder triggering.
research_insights.boundary_risk: Storage cap binds: unconstrained EOQ of 54,484 reduced to 35,789. This increases ordering frequency (~28 vs ~18 orders/year) and raises annual ordering cost slightly, but total cost remains 83% below SAP baseline. If storage capacity increases, order quantity should be revisited toward the unconstrained EOQ.
research_insights.escalation_flag: none — MOQ (3,696) + safety stock (7,492) = 11,188 units, well within the 43,282-unit storage limit. No infeasibility conflict.
